prerequisites: Knowledge of programming with imperative programming languages

learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to design and implement non-trivial relational databases, as well as define and execute queries on data stored in a relational database.
Students will be able to apply the methodologies and technologies learned throughout the course.
Students will be able to evaluate and interpret potential approaches for solving problems related to the design and implementation of a relational database.
Students will be able to communicate the topics covered in the course in a clear, rigorous, and critical manner.
Students will develop the ability to learn methodologies and technologies for the development of relational databases.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to databases and database management systems
Conceptual data models: Entity-Relations model, object model
Relational data model: modeling concepts and notation of the relational model, relational algebra, normalization and normal forms
SQL language: definition of data and integrity constraints, queries, data manipulation, views
Introductory notes on the physical organization of data and indexes
Introductory notes on database security and access control
assessment_rules: The final grade is expressed in thirtieths. The exam consists of a written exam and an oral discussion. The written exam includes conceptual and logical design of a database, SQL operations, and open-ended theory questions and/or exercises. The subsequent oral discussion of the written exam may include exercises to be performed by the computer.
